title: What is the Externalizable interface?
keyPoints: Externalizable gives you full control over what is serialized and how
You implement writeExternal() and readExternal() methods
Unlike Serializable, Externalizable calls the default no-arg constructor during deserialization
You decide exactly which fields to write and read – more efficient, more code
Rarely used in modern Java – JSON/Protobuf provide the same control with better tooling

s1_definition.oneliner: Externalizable gives full control over serialization format. You implement writeExternal/readExternal. Unlike Serializable, it calls the no-arg constructor during deserialization.
s1_definition.profdef:
Externalizable vs Serializable:

- **Serializable:** JVM handles field serialization automatically. No-arg constructor NOT called.
- **Externalizable:** You write `writeExternal()` and `readExternal()`. No-arg constructor IS called. Full control over format.
s1_definition.analogy: Serializable is auto-pilot photocopying – the machine copies everything. Externalizable is manual photocopying – you choose exactly which pages to copy and in what order.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Serializable:    JVM reads/writes all fields automatically
                   Constructor NOT called on deserialize

  Externalizable:  You implement writeExternal/readExternal
                   No-arg constructor IS called on deserialize
                   Full control, more code

  Modern: use Jackson @JsonProperty / @JsonIgnore for fine control
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Externalizable gives full control over serialization by requiring you to implement writeExternal and readExternal. Unlike Serializable, it calls the no-arg constructor during deserialization. It is more efficient but requires more code. In modern Java, JSON libraries provide the same control with better tooling.

One sentence to remember: Externalizable = full manual control over serialization format, requires no-arg constructor, rarely used in modern code.
